chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام about the woman in nifās and how long it is obligatory for her to leave the salat (prayer). He said: “She leaves the salat (prayer) so long as she sees thick fresh blood, up to thirty days. Then when it becomes thin and is yellowness, she performs ghusl and prays, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

key_terms.النُّفَسَاءِ: a woman in the state of postpartum bleeding
key_terms.تَرْكُ الصَّلَاةِ: leaving or suspending the salat (prayer) due to legal impurity
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ يَوْماً: the maximum period of thirty days mentioned in this report
key_terms.صَلَّتْ: she resumed and performed the salat (prayer)
key_terms.صُفْرَةٌ: yellowish discharge indicating a change in the bleeding

ai.seo_question: How long does a woman in nifās leave salat (prayer), and when does she resume it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning nifās and the suspension of salat (prayer) for a postpartum woman. It states that she leaves salat (prayer) while she continues to see fresh flowing blood, up to thirty days, and when the blood becomes thin yellow discharge, she performs ghusl and resumes prayer.
